summary: Session 1 of 2 -- a read-only audit of every cost claim this repo has committed. Walked all 516 committed versions of every docs/session-sets/*/disposition.json (not the 135 surviving ones -- Set 113 S8 repaired its own asserted block 90 seconds after committing it, so a last-version-only audit reports the repair and hides the assertion) and re-priced 265 in-scope schema-v4 sessions with seat_cost. Findings: the recorded cost history is not broadly wrong, it is broadly ABSENT -- only 22 sessions ever authored a cost block, and of the 16 closed sessions priceable today the record under-reports by 13,386.4 credits ($133.86, +27.6%), roughly twice the single $70.24 miss this set was reserved on. Larger still: $3,305.80 of in-repo Copilot consumption is claimed by no session record at all (16.7% attribution rate). Four new findings beyond the reservation: (1) a self-repairing record under-reports its own defect rate; (2) routed_api: measured is unreachable from the producer and appears in 7 committed versions -- a deterministic hand-authorship falsifier Session 2 should ship; (3) routed_seat: measured at close time is not exact, proven by 5 blocks that price higher today, so a close-time reading must label EVERY component a floor; (4) --retrospective from inside your own still-running conversation is also not exact (113 S8: +25.6%), which contradicts seat-cost.md 5.2 and is an owed doc fix. Nothing in a closed session's record was modified.
residuals: LIVE INSTANCE OF THIS SET'S OWN FAILURE, recorded rather than quietly fixed. This session's first disposition.cost was built from CostReport.to_dict() instead of the producer docs/disposition-schema.md names (seat_cost --cost-block / CostReport.to_cost_block). to_dict() omits measured_at and carries store_path, an absolute machine path that has no place in a committed artifact. close_session REFUSED the block and printed exactly which field was malformed -- the same refusal Set 113 S8 met and answered by hand-editing the field until the validator went quiet. This session answered by calling the producer. Two Session 2 inputs follow: (a) the refusal is advisory, so the close still SUCCEEDED with no usable cost record -- the gate reports a malformed block exactly as loudly as a missing one and blocks neither; (b) to_dict() and to_cost_block() are two adjacent methods of which only one is valid here, and nothing in the type system or the call site says so.

The three audit scripts (cost_audit.py, claims_v2.py, cost_classify2.py) live in the session workspace, not the repo: the set declares 'Touches: the set directory only' and three throwaway modules in a docs directory would be worse than the method section in cost-audit.md, which states every input and every rule. Re-deriving the audit means re-writing ~300 lines against a documented method, not recovering a lost one.

router-metrics.jsonl is gitignored machine state and has demonstrably LOST rows it once had (Set 113 S2-S7 and 133 S1-S2 committed blocks quoting Direct-API call counts the surviving file cannot reproduce). Session 2's gate must not treat it as a record of equal standing with session-state.json. Named here, not fixed here.

This session's own cost block exhibits Finding 3: routed_seat comes back 'measured' (exact) at close time while orchestrator_seat correctly comes back 'lower_bound'. It is left as the producer emitted it -- correcting it by hand would be exactly the defect this set exists to stop -- and stands as dogfood evidence for the Session 2 fix.

The $3,305.80 unattributed figure is scoped by the store's own repository column and includes ad-hoc Copilot CLI use in this checkout that was never a workflow session. Nothing in the record separates the two.
